title: Radiation Injuries

source.boundary: Actual Radiation Injuries title at top of right column PDF29/printed47, excluding preceding chapter in left column, through REFERENCES heading and online-reference notice in right column PDF34/printed52, the final PDF page. No individual reference list is supplied in this PDF.
source.verification: Worker checked hash and source; main independently verified all18 term/page matches and visually inspected rendered start/end pages. Selected vocabulary occurrence only, not clinical recommendations, mechanisms or current practice validation.

scope: Eighteen selected vocabulary terms, not exhaustive chapter coverage or a quota. Offline visual-cue candidates only, not medical anchors, narration, scenes or image-generation prompts. Newly recorded does not imply original invention.

source_wording_notes.dirty bombs: Quoted plural phrase in introduction on printed47; punctuation is not part of the selected term.
source_wording_notes.Gray: Capitalized unit name in Table10-2 on printed48; the visual bridge is the ordinary color word, not a unit definition.
source_wording_notes.Becquerel: Capitalized unit name in Table10-2 on printed48.
source_wording_notes.external contamination: Exact phrase in Table10-7 on printed51; not substituted for irradiation or internal contamination.
source_wording_notes.sulfadiazine: Exact word in local radiation injury prose on printed51; partial sulfa-/sulfon- learned cue is shared with Chapter6, not a whole-drug identity claim.
source_wording_notes.Prussian blue: Exact name in Table10-9 on printed51; only blue-color/name association is proposed, not the table's treatment relationships.

entries.cue: Conventional cartoon bomb token visibly covered in dirt.
entries.reason: Familiar adjective/object combination, not a device design, composition, dispersal explanation or an assertion that radioactive material is visible dirt.

entries.cue: Neutral referee standing evenly between two opposing teams, favoring neither side.
entries.cue_scope: Neutral association for the neut- name fragment
entries.reason: Familiar neutral role can support a learned name association without encoding every sound. Not a particle diagram, nuclear mechanism or proof of recognition; may also recall neutrality generally.

entries.cue: Dust-like specks falling out of a suspended cloud onto a model landscape.
entries.cue_scope: Falling-out association in radiation vocabulary context
entries.reason: Economical learned action cue. Falling specks alone can mean ordinary dust or ash; no source, composition, visibility, travel range or hazard map is encoded.

entries.cue: Large plain gray paint swatch beside a gray paint tin.
entries.reason: Exact ordinary word supplies a learned name cue. Color has no quantitative or clinical meaning; not an absorbed-dose definition, conversion or threshold.

entries.cue: Wearable meter badge with a conspicuous small dial clipped to a mannequin's clothing.
entries.reason: Familiar badge/device association is adequate at category level even if it also suggests a staff monitor. Illustrative dial is not a specified instrument design, placement instruction, reading or operational claim.

entries.cue: Recognizable handheld survey meter with a separate cable-connected probe and a prominent dial.
entries.reason: Device recognition need not recover the name from syllables. Not a detector specification, scanning technique or statement that a pictured probe detects every radiation type. Distinguish from the wearable dosimeter cue.

entries.cue: Oversized shield standing between a source token and a mannequin.
entries.reason: Reuses established shield primitive. Not a claim of complete protection or any specific material, thickness, radiation type or equipment recommendation.

entries.cue: Conspicuous contaminant-marker specks on the outside surface of a transparent mannequin, with its interior clear.
entries.reason: Existing outside relation is composed with a body boundary. Specks are artificial mnemonic markers, not visible radiation; no hazard, transfer, exposure or cleaning claim. Newly recorded composition, not a new spatial primitive.

entries.cue: Conspicuous contaminant-marker specks wholly inside a transparent mannequin, with its outside surface clear.
entries.reason: Pairs the existing inside relation with a body boundary. Not absorption, entry route, organ distribution or a claim that internal material is visible; not interchangeable with irradiation alone.

entries.cue: Closed stage curtain concealing a prop whose outline remains faintly visible behind it.
entries.cue_scope: Latent/hidden state plus theatrical phase cue
entries.reason: Familiar concealed state can recall latent after teaching. Not a symptom timeline, prediction, recovery claim or representation of a clinical mechanism; competes with hidden/incubating concepts.

entries.cue: Thin skin-like surface layer visibly flaking and peeling from a study mannequin's forearm.
entries.reason: Familiar action/category rather than forced syllables. Not radiation-specific, diagnostic, a severity scale or a recommendation to peel skin; keep distinct from Chapter7 glove-shaped removal.

entries.cue: Three nearly empty transparent bins containing distinct red-cell, white-cell and platelet study tokens.
entries.reason: Shared low-quantity primitive supports a learned category cue. Not a blood count, diagnostic threshold, production mechanism or radiation-specific finding. Token recognition and distinction from one-cell-line shortage remain untested.

entries.cue: Chromosome-shaped teaching token with two conspicuous pinched centers along the same continuous token.
entries.reason: Simple two-center relationship, not a laboratory image, chromosome assay interpretation, radiation mechanism or dose-estimation claim. Requires learned chromosome recognition; ordinary X silhouettes may obscure the two-center relation.

entries.cue: Shower removing conspicuous surface stains from a protective-suit mannequin.
entries.reason: Reuses existing cleaning/removal candidate. Not an instruction for radiation exposure, proof of suitability, fluid choice, equipment specification or a claim that irradiation alone requires cleaning.

entries.cue: Pile of cracked, rotten eggs with exaggerated stink lines.
entries.cue_scope: Shared sulfur association for the sulfa- name fragment
entries.reason: Reuses the user's sulfur/sulfon egg primitive rather than inventing a forced full-name rebus. Not a claim of drug odor, chemistry, allergy cross-reactivity, indication or equivalence to sulfonylureas; lesson context must provide the particular name.

entries.cue: Conspicuous deep-blue pigment mound beside a paintbrush loaded with the same blue.
entries.prior: New composition sharing the blue-color primitive with methylene blue in docs/chapter-8-cue-audit.json.
entries.reason: Broad learned color/name cue is worth retaining without forcing Prussian into unfamiliar military costume. Color alone cannot discriminate this from methylene blue; lesson context is necessary and a shared lesson would need an additional differentiator. Does not encode the whole name uniquely, compound identity, radionuclide pairing, medical use or a mechanism; blue pigment is not a medication depiction.

entries.cue: Conspicuous stop barrier across a recognizable vomiting bucket.
entries.reason: Reuses established category association as vocabulary only, not a medication selection, clinical mechanism, treatment recommendation or guarantee of benefit.
No economical familiar bridge proposed in this bounded review. Do not force beak/rail syllable repairs merely to fill the unit-name slot. Hold is not a claim that no useful association exists.
